<div class="review-text">
Overland was so good that I bought it twice; once on itch.io as a part of the <a href="https://itch.io/b/520/bundle-for-racial-justice-and-equality">Bundle for Racial Justice and Equality</a>, and then once later so that I could have it in my Steam library to show off to my friends. I strongly believe that this was the most slept-on traditional roguelike of the last several years, holding a special place in my heart alongside <a href="http://www.thegroundgivesway.com/">TGGW</a>.<br>
<br>
The game is somewhat shallow compared to other entries in the realm of squad-control strategy which pile on mechanic after mechanic in a effort to pass volume as depth. But from a design perspective, this keeps the game comfortable to play while also resulting in a much more finely polished experience than the competitors. The game presents interesting situations constantly, and the general gameplay loop is very satisfying.<br>
<br>
But of course, the elephant in the room with Overland is its stunning beauty and environmental quality. This is one of the prettiest games I've ever played, using a relatively simple style which is polished to perfection. The environment also invokes a feeling of dread in the pit of my stomach quite well, which it does well to contrast periodically with whimsical moments, encounters, jokes, and art. <br>
<br>
I strongly recommend this to people new to this sort of game, traditional roguelike players, and squad-based tactics players alike. It goes hand-in-hand with <a href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/590380/Into_the_Breach/">Into the Breach</a> as well, if you liked that game.
</div>
